external_transfers.name: alert_delivery
external_transfers.detail: Alerts carry check names, statuses and — when a failing sample is included — redacted sample values, to whatever webhook or mailbox the operator configured. That endpoint's own location is outside DataQ's knowledge, so this is a transfer whose destination only the operator can attest to.

external_transfers.name: mcp_ai_clients
external_transfers.detail: The /mcp surface serves run results, redacted failing samples and check configuration to whatever AI client holds a valid PAT — Claude Desktop, Copilot, Cursor. The model provider behind that client, and its jurisdiction, are chosen by the token holder and are outside DataQ's knowledge. This is a live transfer path today, not a future one, and it is the more consequential of the two LLM entries here.

external_transfers.name: llm_intelligence
external_transfers.detail: The OUTBOUND direction — DataQ calling a model on its own behalf — is built (ADR 0042) but not configured: no provider, no stored credential, nothing leaves on the feature endpoints' behalf. The admin test probe is independent of this row, though — it can still send a hand-entered draft's fixed test prompt to a real endpoint before anything is ever saved, recorded like any other call. When enabled it is a Ch. V transfer by construction (schema plus masked profiler statistics for SQL generation and check suggestions; RCA narratives also send the triggering check's own observed_value, masked through the same G3 floor, and expected_value, a check-authored threshold never masked; never raw sample rows; local-endpoint option). Listed while absent on purpose: an auditor should see it was considered, not infer its absence. Distinct from mcp_ai_clients above, which is inbound.

external_transfers.name: signin_email
external_transfers.detail: Email-OTP sign-in (ADR 0032) sends one-time codes to user addresses through the configured SMTP relay. It carries account identifiers — personal data under GDPR Art 4(1) — rather than warehouse content, and the relay is operator-chosen.

external_transfers.name: secret_store
external_transfers.detail: Warehouse credentials are held in the 'openbao' backend. Not customer data, but a remote store is a location outside the app's own region if configured that way — and the credentials it holds unlock the systems the customer data lives in.

external_transfers.name: telemetry
external_transfers.detail: Traces and logs to the configured backend. PII is redacted at the logger (core/logging.py), so this carries operational metadata rather than warehouse values — but the sink is chosen by the operator and may sit in another jurisdiction.

external_transfers.name: usage_telemetry
external_transfers.detail: Usage telemetry is OFF (the admin has not opted in). Nothing about how this workspace is used leaves the deployment, and DataQ's authors receive nothing in any state.

external_transfers.name: openlineage_emission
external_transfers.detail: OpenLineage emission is not configured: no run event leaves this deployment. When enabled (OPENLINEAGE_URL, or the library's transport env, with OPENLINEAGE_DISABLED unset) every suite run emits a START and a terminal RunEvent carrying dataset and job names, check names, statuses and aggregate counts — never a failing-row sample — to an operator-chosen catalog. Listed while absent so an auditor sees it was considered.

external_transfers.name: tamper_anchor
external_transfers.detail: No external anchor is configured (TAMPER_ANCHOR=none): the audit hash chain is computed but never leaves the database, so it is only internally consistent — an actor who can rewrite the whole table can rewrite the hashes with it. When enabled (webhook or object_lock), what leaves is the chain head: a SHA-256 hash, a label, the hashed-event count and a timestamp — never an audit event's actor, action or payload.
